title: Profiles of random trees: Limit theorems for random recursive trees and binary search trees
version: Complete 40-physical-page author-hosted manuscript dated 2005-08-11; published Algorithmica 46 (2006), 367–407. Local PDF SHA-256 0f4338a6ea2f075329ca9906febc3c982bc0917ef87baf7c9a41782d377558de.

method_family: Two-parameter profile recurrences; contraction method; moment asymptotics; characteristic-function Berry–Esseen estimate
input_output_interface: Input: a random recursive tree level k with k/λ_n→α, λ_n=max{log n,1}. Output: for α<e a normalized-profile fixed-point limit; the positive moment-convergence assertion for the first m moments when α<m^(1/(m−1)) and all-moment convergence for α∈[0,1]; a derivative limit around k=λ_n with |k−λ_n|→∞ and o(λ_n); and for 1≤k=o(λ_n) a normal approximation with O(sqrt(k/λ_n)) Kolmogorov error.
transfer_assumptions_and_limits: Preserve the RRT insertion rule, level-profile observable, and exact positive α/range gates. The literal negative clause about failure of the next moment in Theorem 1(ii) is internally inconsistent with Corollary 2 and is quarantined as a defective source-local sentence; do not cite it or substitute a general failure threshold. Corollary 1’s variance coefficient vanishes at α=0,1: use Var=o(μ²) from second-moment convergence there, not Var∼0; the α=1 centered fine-scale and α=0 lower-fringe results have their own gates. The BST portion is a separate root-splitting model and has its own α window. Neither model establishes a fixed cyclic leaf-separation pair statistic or covariance without a new encoding and approximation proof.
